indicator: Working-age adults using any generative AI
reference_period: Pooled April 2026 estimate; online waves Jan-Apr 2026 plus rural UP supplement
population_or_denominator: Working-age adults aged 18-64; pooled N=3256; online wave 1 N=1765; rural UP face-to-face supplement N=508; online wave 2 N=983
methodological_note: Weighted by age gender and urbanicity; online recruitment and self-selection may make adoption estimates upper bounds; rural supplement is one-time

indicator: Working-age adults using generative AI at work
population_or_denominator: Working-age adults aged 18-64; same pooled Rutgers sample N=3256
methodological_note: Weighted by age gender and urbanicity; overlaps conceptually with any-use indicator; not an independent measure

indicator: Work hours reportedly saved due to generative AI
population_or_denominator: Employed respondents in same Rutgers tracker
methodological_note: Weighted by age and gender; self-reported time saving, not measured productivity growth; do not interpret as output per hour

indicator: India rank on working-age-population-adjusted Claude use
population_or_denominator: Countries with sufficient observation volume (116); India sample approximately 58000 conversations
source: Anthropic Economic Index India Country Brief
methodological_note: Ordinal and platform-specific ranking; not representative of national AI adoption; do not convert to a cardinal score without a validated measurement model

indicator: Enterprise respondents reporting significant or full AI use
reference_period: Deloitte State of AI in the Enterprise 2026; fieldwork August-September 2025
population_or_denominator: India subgroup N=200 within global survey N=3235; senior leaders; participating organisations already had at least one working AI implementation in daily use
methodological_note: Not representative of all Indian firms; public methodology does not disclose India subgroup weighting or exact wording and response categories behind the 40 percent result
